oneLiner: A dry run of your cafe before it exists: pick a spot, enter a demand range, simulate a Saturday, compare staff or equipment choices, see runway. The founder and the agent edit the same scenario.

audience.primary: First-time cafe founder with a shortlisted spot, a cash figure and rough rent
audience.coOperator: Agent that runs scenarios and explains them

coreQuestion: What would have to happen for this cafe to work?
principles: The language model never computes numbers; it calls actions and explains their results
Every input carries a provenance tag: observed, public, estimate, illustrative
Derived numbers inherit the weakest tag of their inputs
Same seed for every alternative so comparisons are fair
Each feature has a UI, action, AGENTS.md or skill note, and application state
All AI goes through agent chat; Explain sends a prompt to chat, while UI may call deterministic actions
Defaults use published specifications where available, are not tuned to favor a purchase, and the demo shows the model’s actual recommendation

provenanceTags.observed: Measured by the founder or an open count
provenanceTags.public: From public data or a published specification

states.name: Spot picked
states.summary: The founder pins the proposed cafe location. The map shows nearby cafes, offices, colleges and transit as context only.
human: Drop or drag the pin on the map
agent: setSpot with a place name or coordinates
produces: Nearby places list with source and attribution
Coverage-gap notice where map data looks thin
doneWhen: Pin is set and nearby places are drawn
Nothing on screen converts nearby places into customers
states.stale: Moving the pin never changes demand or results by itself.

states.name: Demand entered
states.summary: The founder enters how many customers could arrive per hour, as a low, base and high range, or derives it from a pedestrian count.
human: Enter low, base and high customers per hour
Edit the Saturday curve and opening hours
Optionally enter a pedestrian count and a conversion rate
produces: Hourly arrival range with a source tag on each number
If a count exists: passers-by x conversion = arrivals
If no count: the conversion rate that break-even would require
doneWhen: Every demand number carries a provenance tag
Defaults are labeled illustrative until edited
The required-conversion view works when no count is given
states.stale: Editing demand marks S4, S5 and S6 stale.

states.name: Shop configured
states.summary: Staff, shifts, equipment, menu and money inputs define one scenario. Variants are copies with one change.
human: Add staff and set shifts, for example a second barista from 10 to 12
Set equipment: group heads, grinders, steam wands
Set menu mix, prices, ingredient costs, rent, wages and cash
agent: Create a variant: copy a scenario, change one thing
produces: Scenario: staff pool, shifts, equipment, menu, money inputs
Task list per drink with tagged service times
doneWhen: Two or more scenario variants can exist side by side
Service times are visible and editable with tags
Humans and the agent edit the same scenario fields
states.stale: Editing the shop marks S4, S5 and S6 stale.

states.name: Simulated
states.summary: A seeded simulation of one Saturday, repeated over many runs, with people and machines as shared resources.
human: Press play and watch the Saturday
Scrub the timeline, change speed, choose the seed
agent: runSimulation with scenario, seed and number of runs
produces: Event timeline returned or stored by server actions for UI playback
Animated queue: arrivals, waiting, being served, lost
Wait p50 and p90, orders served, customers lost
Utilization per person and per machine
Named bottleneck: where tasks wait longest to start

sources.name: No external data: deterministic code on scenario inputs

doneWhen: Pure TypeScript simulation runs on the server via actions with no ML model; actions return or store an event timeline for UI playback
When one barista does several tasks, barista time is named as the blocker if it is
states.stale: Results show a stale badge when any input changed after the run.

states.name: Compared
states.summary: Two scenarios on the same arrivals, with deltas and the assumption that could reverse the recommendation.
states.requires: At least two scenarios with fresh simulation results.
human: Change a shift or machine and watch deltas update
produces: Deltas in wait, orders lost, staff cost and cash
Recommendation plus the assumption that could reverse it
Plain-language explanation tied to numbers returned by actions
doneWhen: Both scenarios use the same arrivals
Every number in the explanation traces to an action result
The reversing assumption is named and can be edited in one click
states.stale: Any edit loops back to S3 (edit shop) or S2 (change demand) and the comparison is re-run.

states.name: Runway
states.summary: Break-even and cash over the first months, built from the chosen staff and equipment.
states.requires: A fresh simulation result for the chosen scenario.
produces: Break-even orders per day and the capture rate it implies
Monthly cash view with startup and recurring costs separated
Months of cash under low, base and high demand
doneWhen: One Saturday is never multiplied by 30
Weekday and weekend demand are separate inputs
Faster service adds revenue only if the saved-customers assumption is on
states.stale: Runway recomputes from the latest scenario and simulation.

actions.name: setSpot
actions.does: Set or move the cafe location and load nearby places

actions.name: setDemand
actions.does: Set low, base and high hourly arrivals, curve and opening hours

actions.name: setPedestrianCount
actions.does: Derive arrivals from passers-by times conversion, or return the required conversion

actions.name: configureShop
actions.does: Edit staff, shifts, equipment, menu and money inputs; create variants

actions.name: tagSource
actions.does: Set the provenance tag on any input

actions.name: runSimulation
actions.does: Run the seeded simulation for a scenario

actions.name: compareScenarios
actions.does: Run two scenarios on the same seed and return deltas

actions.name: explainResult
actions.does: Return plain-language reasons built only from action results

actions.name: computeRunway
actions.does: Return break-even and the monthly cash view

nonGoals: Predicting whether a cafe will succeed
More than one cafe or a marketplace of staff and equipment

items.text: Choose single-user demo mode or a seeded demo account; the app opens in the chosen mode and a Bengaluru map snapshot loads from static data, with source and attribution shown.
Founder can enter low, base and high hourly demand plus rent, cash and opening hours.
Every input shows a provenance tag, and derived numbers inherit the weakest tag.
The simulated Saturday animates arrivals, queue, service and lost customers, and shows wait p50 and p90, orders served, customers lost and the named bottleneck.
Same seed gives identical results, covered by a test.
Asking the agent 'barista or grinder?' creates two scenarios that visibly change in the UI.
A manual shift edit (second barista 10 to 12) triggers a re-run and a comparison with deltas in wait, staff cost and cash.
The result names the assumption that could reverse the recommendation.
Runway shows break-even orders per day and a monthly cash view, with weekday, weekend, startup and recurring costs separate. No multiply-by-30.
Shared-barista case: when one person does several tasks, barista time can be named the bottleneck.
Every UI mutation is an action the agent can also call.
Agent edits appear in the UI without a manual refresh, within a couple of seconds, because both use one database-backed scenario store.
The agent states no number that did not come from an action result.
Built with the Agent-Native framework, scaffolded with npx @agent-native/core@latest create; framework use is verified before ranking.
Each feature has a UI, action, AGENTS.md or skill note, and application state.
application_state records the current view, selected scenarios and timeline position; the agent can navigate the UI.
AGENTS.md encodes the domain rules: never compute numbers, always tag sources, use the same seed for comparisons, and name the reversing assumption.
All AI goes through agent chat; Explain sends a prompt to chat. UI may call deterministic actions; no /api routes wrap actions.
Agent tool calls stream visibly in chat, and the user can stop or redirect the agent.
Scenarios, runs and stale flags persist in the SQL database via Drizzle.
Public Clips recording shows the real app in use with nothing mocked; test the public link in a private window for access without login or request. Fabricated demos are disqualifying.
Submitted through the official form, and receipt confirmed.

Project description names every team member and all pre-existing work or templates, libraries and third-party data, says building started on or after October 27, 2026, and identifies what changed during the event.
Submitted before Mon 9 Nov 11:59 PM PT (Tue 10 Nov 1:29 PM IST).
Every team member is 18 or older (or the age of majority, if higher) and eligible; tick the Official Rules agreement and personal-data consent on the form.
Submit early: technical problems do not automatically extend the deadline. The form has one optional Project or GitHub URL field only.
Never put identity, tax or payment documents in the form or demo; non-US winners may face US withholding.
MCP endpoint demonstrated driving the app from an external agent.
Three or more Bengaluru neighborhood snapshots.
Public repository or live deployment link.
Shareable scenario link.
Nearby competitor price level shown from the Zomato subset, clearly labeled as context.
Test a single-station simulation against Erlang-C within a stated tolerance.
Use published specifications for defaults where available, do not tune them to favor a purchase, and show whatever the model recommends in the demo.

architecture.store: Scenario store (PostgreSQL via Drizzle): scenarios, runs and stale flags persist in the database. Use the documented local PGlite option for the local demo and verify restart persistence.
architecture.engines: Pure TypeScript simulator and cash model called by actions on the server; no ML model
architecture.playback: Actions return or store an event timeline for UI playback
architecture.applicationState: Records current view, selected scenarios and timeline position; agent can navigate the UI
architecture.sync: Agent edits appear without a manual refresh, within a couple of seconds
architecture.ai: All AI goes through agent chat; Explain sends a prompt to chat. UI may call deterministic actions. No /api routes wrap actions.
architecture.demoAccess: Start with the Chat template's documented Continue as local dev entry; verify the actual installed template and use a seeded demo account only if required.

openQuestions.question: Which LLM key powers the built-in agent chat, and is there a free route?
openQuestions.status: provider selection and live verification pending
openQuestions.answer: Official setup supports Builder.io, custom provider keys, or local Ollama. Use an already available supported connection and verify a real tool call. No free allowance is assumed.

openQuestions.question: Can the database be SQLite for a local demo, or is Postgres required?
openQuestions.status: answered by official docs; runtime verification pending
openQuestions.answer: Agent-Native uses PostgreSQL through Drizzle. PGlite is the documented local option. Verify startup from empty storage and persistence across restart; do not substitute SQLite.
